title: Rupee soars 69 paise to settle at its eight-month high of 92.16 against US dollar - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
The rupee on Wednesday jumped 69 paise to settle at 92.16 (provisional), the highest level in this year so far, drawing cues from robust buying in domestic equity markets and unabated foreign fund inflows.

Lower crude oil prices also helped the local currency pare all its losses of the current financial year while investors worldwide preferred Indian equities over other assets, forex traders said.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 92.65 and peaked to 92.16 (provisional) against the greenback at the end of the session, up 69 paise from its previous close.

The session's peak was compared to the closing level of 92.28 against the greenback recorded on March 16 this year.

On Monday, the rupee declined from its seven-month high level to close with a loss of 23 paise at 92.85 against the US dollar. The Indian currency market was closed on Tuesday on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev.

The local unit logged a sharp gain of over 1.6 per cent in five back-to-back sessions since the closing level of 94.19 against the greenback recorded on November 13. In the past seven weeks, the Indian currency has recovered nearly 5 per cent compared to its lowest-ever closing mark of 96.88 versus the US dollar seen on October 8.

Anuj Choudhary, Research Analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan, said the rupee jumped on a surge in domestic markets and weak crude oil prices. However, a strong dollar capped sharp gains.

He further said the rupee is expected to trade with a positive bias on strength in the domestic markets and FII inflows.

"Traders may take cues from GDP, weekly unemployment claims and durable goods orders data from the US. USD-INR spot price is expected to trade in a range of Rs 91.95 to Rs 92.55," Choudhary said.

According to Kaveri More, Commodity Technical Analyst at Choice Broking, the sharp rebound in the rupee could extend further, with the next downside targets placed around 91.40–90.

"The rally is supported by strong foreign portfolio inflows of over USD 14 billion in November, renewed foreign bond purchases, easing crude oil prices and measures undertaken by the RBI to improve dollar liquidity and stabilise the currency," More said, adding, "Sustained foreign inflows and softer crude oil prices may therefore remain key factors supporting the rupee's recovery in the near term."

Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was at 103.90, higher by 0.15 per cent, after US Treasury yields slipped as investors moved to safer investments.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.16 per cent lower at $91.55 per barrel in futures trade.

In the domestic equity market, Sensex was trading 1,215.02 points or 1.47 per cent higher at 83,651.01 in afternoon trade, while the Nifty was up 368.15 points or 1.45 per cent at 25,717.60. The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 2,062.22 points to hit the day's high of 84,498.21. The 50-share NSE Nifty surged 602 points to 25,951.65.

Although the benchmark indices ended nearly 2 per cent lower in the preceding session, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought equities worth ₹5,672.99 crore on a net basis on Monday, according to exchange data.

"As investors rotate away from AI-heavy markets such as South Korea, Taiwan and Japan, foreign funds have poured a record of more than $12 billion into Indian equities this month. Together with Brent crude slipping below $90 a barrel, that buying easily outweighed a dollar index near 104," said Rajeev Sharan, Head of Research, Brickwork Ratings.
